distractors.reason: We don't say 'do a coat'. 'Do' is used with tasks: do homework, do the dishes.
We don't say 'make a coat' when we mean putting clothes on. 'Make' means create or produce something.
We don't say 'take a coat' to mean wearing it. 'Take' is used for carrying something somewhere or for taking clothes off: take off your coat.

example_sentence: It is cold, so you should ___ a warm coat.
l1_interference: Polskie słowo „robić” często prowadzi do błędów typu „make a coat” lub „do a coat”. Poprawnie mówimy „wear a coat” (nosić płaszcz), a nie „robić płaszcz” w znaczeniu ubierania się.
explanation: 'Wear' means having clothes, shoes, glasses or jewellery on your body. Think of 'wear' as the state of being dressed, and 'put on' as the action of dressing.

related_collocations.example: Wear a hat in the sun.
Take an umbrella when it rains.
Dress warmly or you will catch a cold.

memory_tip: WEAR = have clothes on your body (coat, hat, shoes) | MAKE = create something (decisions, plans, things)
